To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of correct and incorrect word sequences in expository essays is strongly related to the number of functional units in the essay and the quality of the writing, and that these relationships do not vary as a function of essay length.
curriculum-based measures in writing were significantly related to the quality and completeness of expository writing and that the relationship was stronger for shorter essays than longer essays.

(a) curriculum-based measures are valid indicators of the quality and completeness of middle school students' expository writing, (b) the relationship between the curriculum-based measures and the criterion measures is stronger when the length of the text increases, and (c) curriculum-based measures can detect change in student performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between curriculum-based measures in writing and quality and completeness of expository writing for middle school students.
the development of a curriculum-based assessment of writing that is sensitive to changes in student performance.
the relationship between curriculum-based measures in writing and quality and completeness of student writing.

the curriculum-based measures of CWS and CIWS are valid for middle school students and that they are sensitive to change in student writing performance.
curriculum-based measures in writing provide a valid measure of student performance on expository essay writing.
CWS and CIWS are valid measures of student performance in expository writing.

curriculum-based measures are valid indicators of student performance on criterion measures of written expression.
the curriculum-based measures in this study have a high degree of criterion-related validity.

curriculum-based measures of written expression are valid measures for middle school students and can be useful in identifying students with writing difficulties.
